niche: a Texas clay-soil city's water utility forecasting the utility-side service leaks its crews will repair in calendar 2027, the year its AMI contractor exchanges about two thirds of the city's meters in six months, for the estimated quantities of its 2027 service repair and restoration term contract
answer: TBD at stage 3 (prototype about 1,950 service leak repairs in 2027)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stitches the two work order systems, counts one repair per leak, reads the utility-side boundary correctly and carries the service leaks per service-year of the last two years (or a model of them on each service's material, age and pressure zone) to the 2027 inventory, net of the services the capital program renews, files about 1,100 repairs against about 1,950, because an operated angle valve or setter leaks within weeks about once in a hundred exchanges and the record's routine exchanges carry almost none of what the 2027 mass exchange sets off.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the expected count of service failures in 2027, a buried-asset failure hazard estimated per service from its own repair history with each service's own exposure to a work-induced risk window after a meter exchange; with another field's nouns there is no meter setter operated on an old service, no exchange visit that disturbs it and no risk window after it, so the task stops making sense.
layer1: two work order systems either side of a 2021 CMMS cutover, the legacy one keyed by street address and the new one by GIS service ID
one leak carried on several work orders (investigation, repair, restoration)
a premise-to-service crosswalk that is not one to one (multi-unit premises on one service)
meter history as separate remove and install rows in the CIS
material codes from two GIS conversions
a fiscal year from October to September in the utility's budget against calendar-year counts
stakeholder_role: distribution maintenance planner in the city water utility, sizing the 2027 service repair and restoration term contract

spine.entity: one meter set or removal on a premise in the CIS

world.geography: United States, Texas (a fictional clay-soil city of about 380,000)

driver: Work done on a unit raises the chance that a part attached to it fails in the weeks that follow, and the record spreads such work thinly across every year, so a failure rate read per unit-year carries only the thin history's share of work-induced failures into a window in which most units are worked on at once; the window's failures are each unit's own rate plus each scheduled visit's induced chance, read from the history's visits on each unit's own record.
driver_concrete: An old curb stop or meter setter that is operated when a meter is exchanged leaks within weeks about one time in a hundred, and the record's routine exchanges touch about four meters in a hundred a year, so the service leaks per service-year the history shows carry almost none of the leaks the 2027 AMI exchange of two thirds of the meters will set off; the forecast adds to each service's own rate the induced chance per exchange, read from the leaks on each service in the weeks after its own past exchanges.
stump: A competent solver carries the record's service leaks per service-year (or a model on material, age and pressure zone) to the 2027 inventory and files about 1,100 repairs against about 1,950, because it never reads a service's failures on its own meter exchange visits, which leak within weeks about once in a hundred and which the 2027 AMI contract multiplies about thirteenfold.

differentiation.task125: task125 re-estimates an aggregate on each period's mix of filtered and unfiltered intakes after a recruitment change; task173 adds to each service's own failure rate the induced chance per scheduled meter exchange, a transient risk window after work on the unit itself, with no intake, filter or recruitment
differentiation.task150: task150 projects a unit's count from its own members, steady outside arrivals and sibling transfers; task173 forecasts failures as each unit's own rate plus a risk window opened by work done on it, read from each unit's own past work
differentiation.task501: task501 reads a transmission matrix's eigenvalue under the season's mixing regime; task173 has no transmission or threshold: failures are independent per service, raised for weeks after an exchange visit
differentiation.task132: task132 resets a wear-out curve when a failed item is replaced in its position; task173's exchanged meter is not the failing part: the visit disturbs the old setter and service it sits on, which fail in the weeks after
differentiation.task183: task183 carries each part's own prior failures forward as a frailty; task173's raised risk comes from work done on the unit, not from its failure history, and lasts weeks
differentiation.task149: task149 reads a hazard per unit of working time against how fast engineered work is done; task173's hazard is per service-day, raised in a window after a discrete visit
differentiation.task480: task480 v1 read old meters' under-registration at their exchange (what the meter had recorded); task173 reads the service leaks the exchange visit sets off on the old setter and service, nothing about what the meter recorded
differentiation.task177: task177 v3 read a default almost only through an exit whose forward hazard a second register shows (a behaviour, estimated per sector); task173's trigger is the organisation's own scheduled visit, its forward count filed, the failures it sets off a few per cent of the record's, and the decisive estimate is the transient excess over each service's own baseline in the weeks after its own past visits

lineage.fate: abandoned unregistered on 2026-10-22 (the guard's window blocked it three days; the author chose a fresh draw), then the number was retired after two redraw cells died on code, and reopened by the author on 2026-10-23
lineage.driver: The forward load on a pooled service desk is set by how often a case comes back, which is set by who took its first contact and how long they had been on the desk, so a coming bench far from the record's mix of first-contact takers needs the comeback chance conditioned on each opener's group and tenure.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-23 at stage 4 on Gate F (zip be677673): a blind reader fitted each combined plant's river lift and well per service and landed the call; the next two cells (psychology decision-making, human reliability) died at stage 1 with no card
lineage.driver: A group cut for the first time replaces the lost volume from a second source that shares one meter with the first, so its added draw is the volume times the second source's own cost per unit less the first's, a pair each unit yields only when its metered total is fitted to its own two recorded volumes; reading the meter as one source, or carrying the cost per unit measured on the units cut before, whose second source costs several times as much, misstates the draw several fold.

notes: Architecture 3 of a reopened number. Coding: decisive gap time (the record holds meter exchanges thinly, the forward year massively), population second (the 2027 service-months sit mostly inside the post-exchange window). G2 decisive (the unit the failure rate is read on is each service's own exchange visit and the weeks after it, not the service-year, its route or its street), G7 second (when the induced failures can happen is pinned by an operations file, the AMI deployment schedule), G6 third (the forward year's service-months move to the post-exchange state).
